findings.description: The mechanism that actually closes the r2 blocker cannot tell a correct implementation from the defective one, because V-1 never requires per-case isolation and frames the new porcelain observation as an assertion against the artifact rather than a precondition on the harness. V-1 says 'build a scratch repo with a bare origin per B-4's harness, and run these nine cases' -- one repo, nine cases, no instruction to rebuild or `git clean` between them. V-4 says 'two identically-constructed scratch repos' for its two runs, so the document knows how to demand a fresh repo when it means one; here it does not. The leak that follows is guaranteed rather than incidental: the five dirty cases are dirtied with an untracked file, and the script under test REFUSES, so that file is never committed away and survives any between-case reset short of `git clean -xdff`. From the second case onward every 'clean' case carries it. Measured: under a fully B-4-compliant harness with one reused repo, the CORRECT guard (inserted right after `cd "$SRC"`) violates V-1's new porcelain assertion on A2, B2, C2 and D2 -- a FAIL against work that is right -- and the DEFECTIVE guard (placed after the clean-tree exit at :130-133) violates it in exactly the same four cases while satisfying every other V-1 assertion in all nine. The assertion discriminates good harness from bad harness, not good artifact from bad, and V-1 gives the checker no rule for which it has just observed. B-4 gets this right for its control -- 'if either half misbehaves the harness is broken and every V-1 result afterward is meaningless' -- and V-1 has no equivalent sentence. Fix, two sentences: require a freshly built scratch repo per case (or `git clean -xdff` plus a hard reset between them), and say that a non-empty pre-run porcelain on a clean case means the harness is broken and the run is void, not that the artifact failed.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline 298c8a6, PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin", $STUBS and $HOME outside the scratch repo, dates pinned through setup, one repo reused across cases with markers cleared and a hard reset to the base commit between them (no `git clean`). CORRECT guard: A1 PRE_PORC=[?? drift.txt] EXIT=1 1->1; A2 PRE_PORC=[?? drift.txt] EXIT=1 1->1; B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2 all PRE_PORC=[?? drift.txt] EXIT=1 1->1; E1 PRE_PORC=[AA c.txt] EXIT=1 2->2 -- i.e. all four clean cases violate 'must show it empty' against a correct guard. DEFECTIVE guard (same insertion but after the clean-tree exit), same harness: identical table, all nine EXIT=1, counts and staged paths unchanged. Same defective guard under a fresh repo per case: A2/B2/C2/D2 EXIT=0 1->1, caught by the plain exit assertion. constitution.md:53 ('build a scratch repo ... run these nine cases'), :69-71 (the porcelain assertion), against :98 (V-4's 'two identically-constructed scratch repos') and :150 (B-4's harness-is-broken rule for the control).

findings.description: Revision 4 claims the r2 blocker is 'closed three ways ... Any one would close it'. Measured, that is false for two of the three; only V-1's per-case porcelain assertion is load-bearing. (1) The outside-the-repo bullet closes exactly one realization -- $STUBS/$HOME inside the repo -- and nothing else. (2) The negative control is STRUCTURALLY incapable of catching the leak-between-cases realization, not merely unlucky: the control runs the BASELINE script, which commits the dirty marker away and leaves the repo clean, while the script under test refuses and leaves it behind. So the control's two halves both pass on a harness that will dirty every subsequent clean case. It is also order-dependent in the other direction, and B-4 fixes neither the order of its two halves nor whether they share a repo with the nine cases. This does not reopen the r2 blocker -- the porcelain assertion does catch every realization I could build -- but the 'any one would close it' framing invites a checker to treat the one mechanism that works as redundant, and it is the sentence that will get quoted later as settled. Say instead that the porcelain assertion is the mechanism and the other two are cheap redundancy against specific realizations.
findings.evidence: Measured. Harness fully compliant with B-4 as written ($STUBS=$ROOT/stubs, $HOME=$ROOT/home, both outside the scratch repo; authoritative PATH; osascript record outside the repo), one reused repo, control run first against the baseline at 298c8a6: negative half ctrlNEG_A2 PRE_PORC=[] EXIT=0 1->1, log carries 1 'Nothing to commit' line -- PASSES; positive half ctrlPOS_A1 EXIT=0 1->2 -- PASSES. Then the after-:130-133 guard on the same repo: A1..E1 all EXIT=1 with commit counts and staged paths unchanged -- all nine V-1 exit/count/staged assertions satisfied by a guard that never runs on a clean tree. Only PRE_PORC=[?? drift.txt] on A2/B2/C2/D2 exposes it. Contrast, STUBS_INSIDE realization: caught three ways, the outside-the-repo bullet firing first as a static read of the harness, then the negative control (baseline on A2 printed '==> Committing 2 files', COUNT 1->2, zero 'Nothing to commit' lines), then the porcelain assertion (PRE_PORC=[?? stubs/]). constitution.md:43 ('Any one would close it'), :149 (outside-the-repo bullet), :150 (the two-sided control).

findings.description: Both halves of D-1's check are path-level, so no clause in the document can see an out-of-scope edit INSIDE an allowlisted file -- which is where every remaining non-goal lives. D-1's text carries a within-file requirement ('The push path at :159-182 is correct as written and is not touched') and the Non-goals section names another ('Fixing the pre-existing bare compounds at :88, :122, :137'), and neither has a check anywhere. `git diff --name-only 298c8a6..HEAD` emits file names, and check-diff-scope.py takes an allowlist of paths; both are satisfied by any edit to `dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync`. The r0 audit fixed the committed-vs-working-tree axis of this clause and left the granularity axis, so D-1's own failing example still passes D-1's own check. V-4 incidentally catches the push-default example (an enabled auto-push changes the attached-dirty stream), but catches nothing whose output is unchanged, which is the whole bare-compound class. Fix, one clause-sized line: require that the diff of the script against the baseline contain no removed lines -- `git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync | grep -c '^-[^-]'` must be 0. A guard insertion plus a helper is pure addition, so that costs a correct implementation nothing and turns two prose non-goals into a check.
findings.evidence: Measured on a clone at 298c8a6 carrying two edits the constitution explicitly forbids -- the :137 bare compound converted to `if [ ... ]; then ... fi`, and `${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:-0}` flipped to `:-1` -- committed. `git diff --name-only 298c8a6..HEAD` -> `dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync`, the allowlisted path, nothing else; D-1 passes. check-diff-scope.py takes the same path-prefix allowlist (its own docstring: 'an exact file path, or a directory prefix'), so it passes too. B-1 passes: the added line `if [ "$file_count" != "1" ]; then ...` does not match lint.bats's pattern, and B-1 examines added lines only. V-4 passes for the :137 edit alone: baseline vs :137-edited script, AT_DIRTY and AT_CLEAN, merged stream plus exit code, scratch path and date token normalized -> IDENTICAL in both cases. The removed-line probe on the same diff returns 2, versus 0 for a pure guard insertion. constitution.md:156-157 (D-1 text and check), :184 and :189 (the two unenforced non-goals).

findings.description: The r2 minor is not closed by revision 4's fix, because it normalizes the symptom's visible half and leaves the half the clause forbids normalizing. The `$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)` at :142 goes into the commit MESSAGE, and the message is an input to the commit id. If the two runs straddle a UTC midnight, normalizing the `YYYY-MM-DD` token in the output stream makes the subject lines match and leaves the abbreviated sha on the `[main <sha>]` line different -- and V-4 says 'Nothing else may be normalized, and in particular not the abbreviated sha'. So the clause still fails a correct implementation across a UTC day boundary, at the same roughly-one-second-per-day exposure r2 measured. Cheapest real fix: stub `date` in B-4's harness alongside the other stubs, or pin the token by exporting a fixed value the harness substitutes, so the message is identical by construction rather than normalized after the fact.
findings.evidence: Measured. Two scratch repos, identical trees, identical pinned GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE through setup, commit messages differing only in the date token: `[main bce0983] [auto-sync from That-Air] 2026-08-09 - 1 file` versus `[main fb2dd67] [auto-sync from That-Air] 2026-08-10 - 1 file`. Normalizing YYYY-MM-DD leaves bce0983 != fb2dd67 on a line V-4 forbids normalizing. Confirmed in the real comparison stream: the normalized AT_DIRTY output ends `[main bce0983] [auto-sync from That-Air] YYYY-MM-DD - 1 file`, sha unnormalized by design. constitution.md:98 (normalization list), dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:142.

findings.description: The new placement assertion does not test the proposition revision 4's log says it tests. The log at :46 says 'V-1 asserts its own after-`:128` placement claim instead of leaving it as prose'; the assertion added is that a refusing case's log carries the pre-`cd` phase headings, which discriminates only a guard placed above those phases. All six pre-commit phases echo their headings unconditionally, so a guard sitting at baseline :127 -- immediately BEFORE `cd "$SRC"`, using `git -C "$SRC"`, which is the exact escape the r2 minor named -- emits every heading and passes. Measured: heading count 4 of 4 for the :127 placement, 0 of 4 only when the guard is hoisted above the phases. The assertion is worth keeping (it forbids a top-of-script guard, which would skip the capture phases the incident's machine still needs), but it narrows the unverified window rather than closing it, and the log should say so.
findings.evidence: Measured under the compliant harness, fresh repo per case. Guard at baseline :127 (before `cd "$SRC"`, after all six phases): A1 EXIT=1, A2 EXIT=1, D2 EXIT=1, HEADINGS=4 in every case, and the captured log reads '==> Regenerating VS Code extension list' ... '==> Package drift ...' then '==> Refusing to sync: HEAD is detached'. Guard at baseline :36 (above every phase): A1 and A2 EXIT=1, HEADINGS=0. constitution.md:52 (text: 'places the guard after `cd "$SRC"` at `:128`'), :73 (the assertion), :46 (the log's claim). Phase headings echoed unconditionally at dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:39, 57, 65, 75, 85, 103.

findings.description: V-3 now asserts a datum B-4's stub contract does not require the stub to capture. V-3 requires the recording osascript stub to have been invoked 'with the title `Dotfiles sync failed`', which means the stub must preserve its arguments; B-4 still specifies only 'osascript stubbed to a no-op that records its invocation', with nothing about what the record contains -- the same wording r2 filed the minor against. A harness built strictly to B-4 (`touch "$REC"`) satisfies B-4 and makes V-3 uncheckable. One clause is asking the other for something it was not told to provide. Fix in B-4, not V-3: 'records each invocation's full argument list, which is where V-3 reads the title'.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:91 (V-3: 'assert the recording `osascript` stub was invoked in all nine, with the title `Dotfiles sync failed`') against :146 (B-4: 'osascript stubbed to a no-op that records its invocation, so a test run fires no desktop notifications and V-3's notification half has something to read'). Measured with an argument-recording stub, correct guard, fresh repo per case: exactly one call per refusing case, e.g. A1 -> `-e display notification "Refusing to sync: HEAD is detached. See .../last-sync.log." with title "Dotfiles sync failed"`, and D1 -> the same with 'merge in progress'. The title really is the discriminator: the attached-dirty baseline run records `... with title "Dotfiles committed"` from the bare `notify` at :28-31.

findings.description: Off-by-one in the clause's opening claim, carried since revision 2 and unnoticed by three audits. B-4 says 'Five phases run before `cd "$SRC"` at `:128`'; there are six. The stub list happens to cover all six, so nothing is missing in practice -- but the count is the sentence a worker or checker uses to decide whether the list is complete, and the clause's own principle is that 'every stub is named rather than assumed'. V-1's placement assertion names four of the six headings for the same reason and should say it is naming a subset.
findings.evidence: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync, `grep -n '^# ---- Phase'`: :38 VS Code extension list, :52 Claude plugin manifests, :64 chezmoi re-add, :71 strip machine-local keys / Normalizing Claude settings, :82 template drift, :102 package drift -- six -- then :127 commit + push. Six matching `echo "==>` headings at :39, 57, 65, 75, 85, 103, all unconditional. constitution.md:142 ('Five phases'), :73 (four headings named).

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, run cold as asked: the negative half of the new two-sided control does print the exact string the clause names, and creates no commit. Baseline script at 298c8a6, case A2 (detached HEAD, clean tree), authoritative PATH, $STUBS and $HOME outside the scratch repo, dates pinned through setup.
findings.evidence: EXIT=0, `git rev-list --count HEAD` 1 -> 1, staged paths [] -> []. Full merged stream, verbatim final line: '==> Nothing to commit. Already in sync.' preceded by the six phase headings and their skip lines. Log at the redirected $HOME carries exactly 1 'Nothing to commit' line and 0 refusal lines. constitution.md:150.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the r2 blocker itself is closed. The r2 attack, rebuilt from scratch -- a guard identical to a correct one except placed after the clean-tree exit at :130-133, run under a harness that silently dirties the scratch repo -- is caught. Under r2's own realization ($STUBS and $HOME inside the repo) all three of revision 4's mechanisms fire, in this order: B-4's outside-the-repo bullet first, since it is a static read of the harness before anything runs; then B-4's negative control, which the clause requires to run before any V-1 case; then V-1's per-case porcelain assertion. Under the harness realization the outside-the-repo bullet permits, only the third fires -- see the B-4 major above.
findings.evidence: Measured. STUBS_INSIDE harness, defective guard: all nine cases EXIT=1 with counts and staged paths unchanged, i.e. the r2 pass reproduced; PRE_PORC=[?? stubs/] on A2/B2/C2/D2 and [?? drift.txt;?? stubs/] on the dirty ones. Same harness, baseline: A1 EXIT=0 1->2; A2 EXIT=0 1->2 printing '==> Committing 2 files' and committing stubs/chezmoi, stubs/osascript and home/.local/state/dotfiles/last-sync.log -- the negative half fails loudly. Compliant harness, fresh repo per case, defective guard: A2/B2/C2/D2 EXIT=0, caught by the plain exit assertion alone. constitution.md:43, :71, :149-150.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, attacked for the new vacuity the orchestrator asked about and none found. Naming all four committed cases does not by itself constrain what they assert, but the mutation step now has a non-empty set to quantify over and does the constraining: a blocked-state case asserting nothing, or asserting something unconditionally true, stays `ok` under its detector's deletion and fails B-3; a case red today for an unrelated reason fails D-2's `bats tests/` before B-3 is reached; and the cross-condition ('the others, including the attached case, stay green') catches a case that goes red under every mutation. Two residuals, neither worth a severity. B-3 says 'the committed test file' and `bats tests/<new file>`, singular, which is underspecified if the worker splits cases across files or appends to an existing one. And B-3 does not mandate the `.git/MERGE_HEAD` construction V-1 mandates, so the committed merge case may encode a different contract than the checker's probe -- harmless, because a mismatch between the worker's construction and the worker's own detector goes red in the worker's own suite.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:134 (the four named cases) and :136 (the mutation step and its cross-condition), against :67 (V-1's mandated `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD`) and :164 (D-2's `bats tests/` exits 0). Measured for the underlying premise: the unguarded baseline exits 0 on all nine blocked cases and on both attached cases, so every blocked-state case has something to flip, and no per-detector mutation touches the attached path.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND on the question asked: V-3's own nine-case probe does not reintroduce the r2 coupling from the other direction. What r2 objected to was V-3 reading a datum out of another clause's fixed record; running its own probe under B-4's harness is an instruction V-3's checker can execute alone, the same shape V-2 and V-5 already use and which r2 accepted. The cost is a duplicated harness build, not a dependency. The probe's premise also holds: in a refusing run the refusal is the only osascript caller, because the template-drift `notify` at :97 needs `chezmoi status` output and B-4 stubs it empty. V-3 inherits V-1's isolation gap, though -- see the V-1 blocker -- since it runs V-1's nine cases.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:91 against :84 (V-2's 'from V-1's nine runs') and :107 (V-5's 'from V-1's clean-tree cases'). Measured, correct guard, fresh repo per case: exactly one recorded osascript call per case, title 'Dotfiles sync failed' in all nine, and zero calls in the clean attached run. dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:96-97 (the drift notify, unreachable under the empty `chezmoi status` stub).

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: citations, floors and the borrowed regex re-derived from the artifacts rather than diffed against the revision log. Every script line the document cites resolves, the eight per-file floors match, `bats --count tests/` is 120 at the baseline so D-2's '>120' is a real floor, and B-1's fenced pattern is byte-identical to the one lint.bats applies. B-1's scoping claim also holds: lint.bats's guarded surface is `$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/*.bats` plus helpers.bash plus mutation-check.sh, which excludes the sync script -- and, worth noting for the worker, INCLUDES any new tests/*.bats file, so the new test file is lint-covered through D-2 even though B-1 is not scoped to it.
findings.evidence: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync is 182 lines; :16 `set -euo pipefail`, :18 `SRC="$(chezmoi source-path)"`, :26 `exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1`, :28-31 notify, :33-36 notify_fail, :66 `chezmoi re-add`, :87-95 the drift loop with `|| continue` at :90, :128 `cd "$SRC"`, :130-133 the clean-tree exit, :142 the commit subject, :153-158 the push rationale, :159-182 the push path. Floors by `/usr/bin/grep -c '^@test'`: apps 18, doctor 11, font 44, install-failures 17, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, lint 1, packages 13; `bats --count tests/` = 120. B-1 pattern compared programmatically against tests/lint.bats -> equal, True. tests/apps.bats:73 `export PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin"`; tests/doctor.bats:62 `export PATH="$STUBS:$PATH"`.

findings.description: Read cold as a worker would, one consequence of Phase 0 override 1 that no clause names and the worker should not have to infer. Because the guard sits after `chezmoi re-add`, a refusal happens AFTER the capture phases have already written $HOME's changes into the source dir. On the incident's machine that means every daily run against a detached HEAD leaves fresh uncommitted captures in the source tree and then refuses -- correct behaviour under the spec ('before staging anything'), and the deliberate price of keeping the capture phases running, but it is the behaviour a reader of the constitution would be surprised by. V-1's placement paragraph justifies the position only as 'the phases the incident's machine still needs to run'; one clause saying the refusal is expected to leave the source dir dirty would close the gap between what the document requires and what the worker will observe.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:9 (Phase 0 override 1), :73 (placement assertion). dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:64-69 (`chezmoi re-add`, unguarded, before :128). Measured in every refusing case: the run reaches '==> Capturing live $HOME changes back into source' before the refusal line.
